we need to do this:
12:00 : The Noon Curveball is live. Stop, checkpoint, restart your agent.
Bengaluru Tech Week

Teams,

The Noon Curveball is now live. A new constraint has been introduced for every track.

Before you change any code:
Stop implementation.

Commit your last stable version.

Confirm Entire created a Checkpoint (entire status).

End your current agent session.

Read your track's card below.

Start a FRESH agent session.

Use your pre-curveball Checkpoint to reconstruct your intent, architecture, completed work, and open risks in that new session.

Run Entire Graph impact analysis BEFORE editing.

Implement and test the new requirement.

Create a final Checkpoint explaining your revised design.


Update your implementation, add appropriate tests, and preserve existing working behaviour.

Your final submission must explain what assumption changed, how your design changed, and why the new result is safe.


TRACK 1: PRIVACY BOUNDARY
Your Checkpoint-native experience must now work with sensitive repositories.

The security team has introduced these requirements:

Raw prompts and transcripts must not be sent to a new external service.

The product must continue to provide useful output when sensitive fields are redacted or unavailable.

Existing local functionality must continue to work.

The interface must clearly distinguish between complete and incomplete context.

You must include at least one test using redacted or missing Checkpoint data.

Use Entire Graph to identify every code path affected by this privacy boundary.

Your product must never present incomplete context as a complete or authoritative result.

A redacted Checkpoint fixture is attached.


TRACK 2: GRAPH IS EVIDENCE, NOT AN ORACLE
Your Graph-powered experience has encountered a repository using dynamic dispatch, generated code, reflection, or another pattern that static analysis cannot fully resolve.

The new requirements:

The product must not present incomplete Graph relationships as certain.

It must identify when analysis may be partial.

It must provide a safe fallback or verification path.

Existing behaviour for fully resolved code must continue to work.

You must include a test or fixture representing incomplete analysis.

Use Entire Graph to identify which parts of your implementation consume relationship, impact, or semantic diff evidence.

Users and agents must be able to tell apart:

Confirmed structural evidence

Heuristic or incomplete evidence

Claims that require source or test verification

A partial analysis repository fixture is attached.


TRACK 3: THE AGENT CHANGED ITS FORMAT
The agent or workflow you integrated has released a new transcript and lifecycle event format. Existing users still produce the original format.

The new requirements:

The integration must support both the original and the new format.

Unknown events must not crash the integration.

An incomplete transcript must produce a partial result, not a corrupted or discarded session.

Existing Checkpoint behaviour must remain compatible.

Tests must cover:

Original format

New format

Unknown events

Incomplete input

Use Entire Graph to identify every parser, lifecycle handler, summary path, and Checkpoint writing path affected.

Do not duplicate the entire implementation for each format.

A JSONL fixture representing the new format is attached. Check with your mentor that you have the one matching your integration.


HOW THIS IS SCORED - 15 POINTS
We are looking for:

A fresh session that reconstructs earlier work from Checkpoint context

Graph impact analysis run before editing

A clear statement of which assumption the curveball invalidated

A focused revision that preserves existing behaviour

Tests for the new behaviour

A final Checkpoint explaining the adaptation

Graph use that happens after implementation, or an explanation given verbally rather than captured in context, scores in the partial band.

Curveball protocol — I'll handle the pre-restart steps in this session: check the working tree, commit the last stable state, and confirm Entire made a checkpoint. Then this session ends and you start fresh.
